title: Consolidate CI caching, slim builder images, and upgrade linters/toolchains
creator: Ethan Kim
description:
Background:
We have recurring CI flakiness and long cold build times across repos (backend Go services, Node SDKs, and some Python tooling). Recent audits (ENG-4827, ENG-7219) flagged duplicated Docker base images, inconsistent cache keys, and outdated linters/typecheckers that block builds.

Goal:
Consolidate and modernize CI build pipelines to reduce median pipeline time by ~40% on cold runs and by ~60% on warm runs, reduce cache misses, and eliminate common flake classes caused by mismatched tool versions. This ticket covers cross-repo build cache strategy, slimming/standardizing builder images, and upgrading key dev toolchains (ESLint/Prettier/TypeScript, Go toolchain, Python lint/test deps).

Success criteria (acceptance):
- Cold build median time reduced by >=35% across representative CI jobs (api-backend, sdk-js, infra-scripts).
- Warm build/cache-hit times reduced by >=60% where remote cache is effective.
- >=90% of CI jobs use the new standardized builder images or base image layers.
- Linter and typecheck jobs run deterministically with pinned versions; no flakiness introduced by version drift.
- Migration docs and rollout plan published; small set of repos migrated in this cycle and rest scheduled.

Out-of-scope for this ticket: full migration of all private on-prem pipelines (follow-up ticket), changing runtime base images for customer-facing containers (separate security review).

Technical approach:
1) Standardize builder images:
   - Create minimal multi-stage builder images per language family (go-builder: go1.21, node-builder: node20, python-builder: python3.11) with common OS layer (debian-slim) and shared dev tools (git, ca-certificates, jq).
   - Publish images to Redwood internal registry with immutable digests and short-lived tags for daily builds.
   - Document image tags and pinning policy for repos.

2) Centralized remote build cache:
   - Prototype BuildKit remote cache backed by our registry (buildx with --cache-to/--cache-from) for Docker layers and a simple S3-backed artifact cache for non-container artifacts (pip wheels, node_modules tarballs).
   - Integrate registry-backed layer caching into GitHub Actions workflows and Jenkins self-hosted runners.

3) CI cache key hygiene and consolidation:
   - Standardize cache key format: repo:${{hash(files affecting deps)}}:toolchain:${{tool-version}}.
   - Replace ad-hoc actions/cache setups with shared reusable workflows (GH actions) that the monorepo and service repos import.

4) Toolchain upgrades and pinning:
   - Upgrade ESLint, Prettier, and TypeScript to current LTS minor versions in sdk-js; add lockfile verification step.
   - Move Go builds to go1.21 toolchain, enable go.work for multi-module repos where applicable.
   - Pin Python dev deps (black, flake8, isort, mypy) and switch to wheel caching for faster installs.

5) Parallelization and job pruning:
   - Identify redundant matrix axes and combine jobs where possible.
   - Add conditional job runs for PRs touching docs or docs-only changes to avoid unnecessary builds.

Migration and rollout plan:
- Week 1 (this ticket): Build standardized images, publish to registry, implement shared GH action for caching. Migrate 2 pilot repos: sdk-js and infra-scripts.
- Week 2: Migrate api-backend and one Go service, add registry-backed BuildKit cache on runners, run performance comparison jobs.
- Week 3: Address edge cases, publish migration guide, schedule remaining repos.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Cache poisoning or stale caches causing subtle build breakages. Mitigation: Add cache invalidation policy, and force-full rebuild on base-image changes; include digest in cache key for builder-image changes.
- Risk: Upgrading linters introduces many autofix changes. Mitigation: Run upgrades behind opt-in branch and provide eslint --fix codemods PRs for reviewers; preserve CI pass for existing branches.
- Risk: Self-hosted runners with old docker/buildkit versions. Mitigation: Detect runner capability and fall back to local caching or queue upgrade of runner images.

Metrics to track:
- Median pipeline duration (cold/warm) pre/post per repo (record baseline by 2026-03-09).
- Cache hit ratio for layer cache and artifact cache.
- Number of CI failures attributable to tooling version drift.

Artifacts and links:
- Migration doc draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/ci/build-cache-migration (draft)
- PoC repo for buildx cache: github.com/redwood-inference/ci-cache-poc/pulls/12
- Image registry: registry.redwood.ai/ci-builders

Notes: coordinate with infra on runner upgrades and security on image scanning before GA publish.
comments: 2026-03-11 - Aisha Patel: Started building node-builder image. Initial Dockerfile uses node:20-slim + git/jq. Local smoke tests passed for sdk-js pilot.
2026-03-12 - Priya Desai (Infra): Spun up a staging registry namespace for ci-builders and enabled immutable digest retention for published images.

2026-03-13 - Ethan Kim: Added reusable GH action 'redwood/ci-cache@v1' that implements standardized cache-key logic and supports buildx remote cache. Seeking review from ENG-4827 owners for integration points.

2026-03-14 - Aisha Patel: Pilot migration for sdk-js created (PR #423). Observed 2.1x speedup on warm runs; identified flaky step relating to npm ci lockfile mismatch—adding lockfile verification step.
2026-03-14 - Security (review): Scanned initial images; found 2 low severity OS CVEs scheduled for patch in next base image refresh. Security approves pilot with patch timeline.
notes: This ticket is intentionally cross-repo. Coordinate with SDK owners and Infra before enforcing the new reusable workflows. Avoid sweeping autofix merges during the pilot window.
next_steps: 1) Finish node-builder and go-builder images + publish digests. 2) Merge reusable action PR and flip on for sdk-js pilot. 3) Validate cache hit ratios and measure timing, report back with numbers and follow-up plan.
